solutions.check: 28 entries verified against the grid (lengths, crossings, linked-clue mapping)

clue.text: Hunt involved with barmy broadcast: plausible-sounding rubbish

indicators.note: to broadcast seed is to scatter it widely, so the letters are strewn into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A politician called Hunt gets caught up in a crazy broadcast full of believable nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcast' looks like a noun about a programme, but it is the instruction to mix up the two words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: An urban myth is a widely repeated story that sounds credible but is untrue, which is exactly believable nonsense.

clue.text: Fact: America is rank

parts.note: a stat is a statistic, a recorded fact
US is the standard abbreviation for the United States

explanation.surface: A political jibe: the truth is that America stinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rank' reads as an adjective meaning foul, but here it is the noun meaning position in a hierarchy.
explanation.definitionFit: Status and rank are synonyms for a person's standing or position within a social or professional order.

clue.text: Criticize city mired in sexual activity

indicators.note: something mired is stuck deep inside a bog, so one piece sits within another

parts.note: SM is sadomasochism
LA is Los Angeles

explanation.surface: Condemning a city that has sunk into debauchery.
explanation.walkthrough: The city is not a British one: LA, short for Los Angeles, goes inside S and M.
explanation.definitionFit: To slam someone is informal for attacking them harshly in words, a common newspaper synonym for criticise.

clue.text: Love quota, the speechmaker's thing

parts.note: love is nil in tennis scoring, written as the round letter
a ration is a fixed allowance or share

explanation.surface: A politician's set allowance of affection is the stock in trade of anyone giving speeches.
explanation.walkthrough: Love as zero comes from tennis scoring.
explanation.definitionFit: An oration is a formal public address, so delivering one is what someone who makes speeches does.

clue.text: Winehouse framing arsehole associated with English establishment

indicators.note: a frame goes all the way round a picture, so one piece surrounds the others

parts.note: Amy Winehouse was the English soul singer
a cad is a dishonourable man, a rotter
E is the standard abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: Amy Winehouse is pictured being set up by some lout from the English establishment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arsehole' sounds too crude for a crossword word, but it is just a cad, an old-fashioned word for a scoundrel; the singer's first name does the framing.
explanation.definitionFit: An academy is a school or institution of learning, an example of an educational establishment.

clue.text: President, not finished with America, recruits conservative faction — brainwave!

indicators.note: something not finished lacks its ending, so the final letter is dropped
to recruit is to take people into a body, so one piece is taken inside another

parts.note: Joe Biden, the US President, with his last letter removed
A is a common abbreviation for America
the right is the conservative wing of politics

explanation.surface: A US president, his job undone, enlists a right-wing group, and someone hails it as genius.
explanation.walkthrough: BIDEN loses its N, A is added, and RIGHT goes in after the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A brainwave is a sudden clever thought, and a bright idea is the everyday phrase for the same inspired notion.

clue.text: Terrible slog to cover ultimately unfair debt (grand)

indicators.note: a cover goes over and around something, so one piece wraps the other
something terrible is in a dreadful state, so the letters end up disordered

parts.note: taken as written before rearranging

parts.note: the last letter of the word
an IOU is a written acknowledgement of a debt: I owe you

explanation.surface: A grim grind of work is needed to pay off an unjust debt of a thousand pounds.
explanation.walkthrough: '(grand)' looks like slang for a thousand pounds attached to the debt, but it is the definition. An IOU is a note saying 'I owe you'.
explanation.definitionFit: Grand and glorious both describe something magnificent, splendid and impressive in scale.

clue.text: State aid squandered by House

indicators.note: squandered money is scattered and wasted, so these letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written before rearranging
HO is the standard abbreviation for house

explanation.surface: Government assistance wasted by the House of Representatives.
explanation.walkthrough: House, capitalised to suggest Congress, is just its abbreviation HO.
explanation.definitionFit: Idaho is one of the fifty states of the USA, in the Pacific Northwest, so it is an example of a state.

clue.text: Arse let out with end of trouser snake

parts.note: both are insults for a contemptible person

indicators.note: out can mean wrong or not in order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written before rearranging

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter, so just that letter is taken

parts.note: the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A schoolboy smut: a fart released, along with the 'trouser snake', slang for the penis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trouser snake' looks like one phrase, but 'snake' alone is the definition. 'Arse' is an insult for a person, as is RAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Rattler is the informal short name for a rattlesnake, the American viper with a noisy tail.

clue.text: Went round with corrupt cleric, initially defrocked

indicators.note: corrupt means spoilt or perverted from its proper form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written before rearranging

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the first letter is used

parts.note: the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: Someone did the rounds with a crooked priest who was stripped of holy orders.
explanation.walkthrough: The first letter of 'defrocked' joins the cleric's letters before they are all rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To circle is to move around something in a ring, so circled is a past-tense synonym for went round.

clue.text: Power-driven, advanced, spread out and screwed

parts.note: A is a standard abbreviation for advanced

indicators.note: to spread something is to distribute it differently, so the letters are rearranged into a new order

parts.note: taken as written before rearranging
to mate is to have sex, which screwed also means

explanation.walkthrough: 'Spread out' looks like one phrase, but 'out' is the fodder and 'spread' rearranges it.
explanation.definitionFit: Automated machinery works by itself under its own mechanical or electrical power rather than by hand.

clue.text: Tackle bent back — no end to the thickness

indicators.note: having no end means the final letter is removed
something bent back is turned to face the other way, so the letters run in the opposite direction

parts.note: rig is gear or equipment, like fishing tackle
the word with its last letter removed

explanation.walkthrough: Tackle, as in fishing gear, is RIG; the 'tackle' innuendo is a red herring.
explanation.definitionFit: Girth is the measurement around the middle of something, so it describes how thick or broad it is.

clue.text: Frontman is (IMO) one to ferment fake news

indicators.note: to ferment is to stir up and agitate, so the letters are churned into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: In my opinion, the band's frontman, or the front man of a party, is a spreader of fake news.
explanation.walkthrough: IMO is internet shorthand for 'in my opinion', but here its three letters simply go into the mix.
explanation.definitionFit: Fake news is false information presented as fact, which is what misinformation means.

clue.text: In complete denial when nitrogen added to his illicit rum — left to withdraw

indicators.note: to withdraw is to pull out, so the letter for left is removed

parts.note: N is the chemical symbol for nitrogen

indicators.note: rum as an adjective means odd or strange, so the letters become a strange arrangement

parts.note: taken as written before rearranging
the word with one L, for left, taken out

explanation.surface: Someone refusing to admit anything, while their bootleg rum has been dosed with nitrogen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rum' looks like the drink but is the adjective meaning odd. L, for left, leaves the fodder, and N goes on the front.
explanation.definitionFit: A nihilist rejects all beliefs and values outright, so nihilistic describes a total refusal to accept anything.

clue.text: Rare rains ruptured behind

indicators.note: something ruptured is burst apart, so these letters are broken up and reassembled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Unusual downpours that burst out of the sky, with a cheeky hint at a backside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Behind' tempts as a noun for the bottom, but it means late with payments.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in arrears means owing overdue payments, so you are behind with what you should have paid.

clue.text: Ratty Conservative, having no alternative, accepts draw

indicators.note: to accept is to take something in, so one piece is placed inside another

parts.note: TORY with OR removed

indicators.note: having none of something means it is taken away

to etch is to draw by engraving

explanation.surface: An irritable Tory with no other options agrees to a drawn match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Draw' suggests a tied match, but it is the verb for making a picture, as etching does. The alternative is the little word that offers a choice.
explanation.definitionFit: Ratty is British informal for irritable and short-tempered, which is also what tetchy means.

clue.text: Duck holds bear up (not taking the piss)

indicators.note: to hold something is to grip it inside, so one piece goes within the other

explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking the piss' is British slang for mocking, but here 'piss' is slang for alcohol, as in 'on the piss'.
explanation.definitionFit: A teetotal person abstains from alcohol entirely, so they never drink booze, slangily called piss.

clue.text: Sheeran is no flipping innovator

clue.text: Possible pot victim has to throw rest out

clue.text: Bizarre Fuhrer's exclusive possession?

second meaning: the wartime song claims Hitler had only got one testicle, an unpaired one

explanation.walkthrough: The British wartime song 'Hitler Has Only Got One Ball' supplies the joke: his only ball is an odd one. The question mark flags the whimsy.
explanation.definitionFit: Oddball works as an informal adjective for strange or eccentric, and split in two describes a single unmatched testicle.

clue.text: Sense of optimism, as a result of grope by wicked female player

an actor plays a part

clue.text: Can Labour finally overcome Left?

explanation.walkthrough: 'Can' looks like a verb opening a question, but it is the noun, American slang for a lavatory. 'Labour' and 'Left' are not the party and its wing.

clue.text: Upper-class coffee houses jibe

clue.text: Mad Conservative leader taking on Jonathan?

clue.text: More lowly than a writer? Make sure you get your Eye regularly!

clue.text: Enclosure: cocaine (mature)

clue.text: Cloth stuck into tool — tender!

clue.text: Real stupid, squeezing say, opening of willy stocking?
